title: Bay Reassigned, No Reason Logged
body: The lunchbox sits on a family manifest, its name column penciled in last, the headcount line still open. The key ring beside it is stamped for a bay that ran co-op orders every spring, now crossed out for a different one.
rival_reading: A warehouse could reassign the same bay for an ordinary co-op shipment and still need a late name added for whoever signed for it; a crossed-out bay number does not by itself show an evacuation failed.
gloss: A family manifest with its headcount left open sits beside a loading bay reassigned from co-op orders.

title: Mix Ratio Written Over A Curfew Notice
body: A curfew notice, patrol shift times still printed down one side, has a mix ratio scrawled across it in a different hand, three parts to one. The bucket beside it is rinsed, a chalky ring left at the waterline.
rival_reading: A curfew notice reused as scratch paper for a route sheet is exactly what an overworked relief desk would do; the ratio jotted over it could just as easily be a cleaning mix, not evidence a farm chemical malfunctioned.
gloss: A mix ratio is scrawled over a curfew notice that still lists patrol shift times.
